data.why: The app's own 'Validation lab' tab calls make_synthetic_cluster() in-process to generate a light image and a 24-model kappa ensemble on demand, so no files need to be prepared; the 'Official HFF' tab would require fetching ~960 MiB of real STScI FITS products via a CLI step with network access the running server will not have, so it is out of scope.

goals: Generate a synthetic light/mass pair with a known injected offset and confirm the audit recovers a centroid offset and discrepancy map consistent with the injected truth
Read the resulting diagnostics (centroid offset, model fractional spread, robust excess area) and judge whether they would indicate a genuine mass-light mismatch versus noise
Adjust the light-proxy smoothing scale and the ensemble discrepancy threshold and observe how the discrepancy map and warnings change
Export the evidence receipt (JSON) and the discrepancy-score FITS map as artifacts of the audit
Upload a pair of co-registered science-image and convergence FITS files and check that mismatched grids or missing WCS are rejected rather than silently resized

review.summary: The tree describes LensAudit's purpose well (auditing mass–light offsets without treating an overlay as a detection), its features are sized well, and most cited screens show what the nodes claim. It needs fixes before filing: the score-map outline is wrongly described as following the threshold, the seed comparison mixes settings, two export nodes cite screens that show nothing, and the real-data and upload audit paths (with their stop and warning branches) are missing.
